sections.content:
<tool_call>
<function=python>
<parameter=code>
# Let's explore the state space more systematically
# First, let's see how many distinct states each pink position can take
# by cycling UP repeatedly and recording patterns

def extract_pattern(lines, rstart, rend, cstart, cend):
    pattern = set()
    for r in range(rstart, rend+1):
        for c in range(cstart, cend+1):
            if lines[r][c] == 'B':
                pattern.add((r-rstart, c-cstart))
    return frozenset(pattern)

# Get top patterns for comparison
ascii = current_frame.ascii
lines = ascii.split('\n')
top_patterns = {}
for ri, (rstart, rend) in enumerate([(4,10), (13,19), (22,28)]):
    for ci, (cstart, cend) in enumerate([(12,18), (22,28), (35,41), (45,51)]):
        pat = extract_pattern(lines, rstart, rend, cstart, cend)
        top_patterns[(ri, ci)] = pat

# Cycle UP at position 0 and record all states
# First go to position 0 (should already be there)
states_at_0 = []
for i in range(20):  # Try up to 20 UPs to find cycle
    ascii = current_frame.ascii
    lines = ascii.split('\n')
    pat = extract_pattern(lines, 51, 57, 14, 20)
    states_at_0.append(pat)
    
    # Check if this matches any top pattern
    match = None
    for (ri, ci), tpat in top_patterns.items():
        if pat == tpat:
            match = (ri, ci)
            break
    
    if i < 5 or match:  # Print first 5 and any matches
        print(f"  UP x{i}: match={match}")
    
    # Check if we've cycled back
    if i > 0 and pat == states_at_0[0]:
        print(f"  Cycle detected at {i} steps")
        break
    
    action(['UP'])

print(f"\nTotal unique states at pos 0: {len(set(states_at_0))}")
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
